newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: INTERVIEW- Digital cuts prices in Asia.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW- Digital cuts prices in Asia.

text.p: Digital Equipment Asia Pacific Pte Ltd's latest price cuts on its Alpha systems and components in Asia will not affect profit margins, Mitch Hall, Digital's director for servers in Asia Pacific, said on Tuesday.
"The overall company's (gross) margins are in the 30-35 percent range right now and will continue to be in that range, if not higher," Hall told Reuters in a telephone interview.
He said the price cuts, coupled with Digital's technical and manufacturing efficiencies, would help it gain market share, offsetting any negative impact the price cuts had on margins.

In response to increasing demand for Digital's 64-bit UNIX solutions, Digital announced last week an aggressive pricing strategy in Asia, where customers can get four times the memory content and faster speed for similar pricing.
Citing an example, Hall said systems with 128 megabytes of main memory would be priced similar to those with 512 megabytes.
The reductions would offer savings of 30-35 percent on certain Alpha systems and memory options.
Hewlett Packard and Sun Microsystems were among the targeted UNIX competitors.

"The new prices make the AlphaServer 4100 systems 34 percent more affordable than a comparable Sun UltraEnterprice 4000 system. The AlphaServer 1000A system is now priced to compete head-on with Compaq 2500," said Hall.
Hall said the move would hopefully see Digital's market share in Asia grow "by several points".

Industry estimates put Digital's market share in Asia between 11 percent to slightly over 20 percent, varying with the country. In Malaysia and Indonesia, Digital has about 20 percent of market share, Hall said.
For the second quarter ended December 1996, Digital's net profit fell sharply to US$31.9 million from US$148.8 million in the same period previously.
Since the launch of the products three and a half years ago, Digital had shipped over US$8 billion worth of Alpha systems and components, Hall said.
Asia presently accounts for 20-25 percent of Digital's global revenue.
Digital was not expected to announce any new price cuts in its other products in the near-term but Hall said it might make some marketing changes in its storage products over the next two months.
